# Exact obstruction to a normal-only critical boundary overlap test

This example concerns the concrete deformation interface in `candidate 92bb4f0b51f51e22`. It has genuine globally critical caps, a complete integer base, and strict exclusion of heavy fibers. Nevertheless potentials depending only on the continuous boundary normal cannot attain the proposed `Gamma_d/k` boundary overlap. It is not a counterexample to OC, or to a test allowed to depend on the integer base and boundary point.

## 1. Actual compatible fibers

Set `n=3`, `d=2`, `L=8`, `delta=1/800`, and

    P={0,1}^2 times {-4,-3,...,4}.

At every base `(0,0,j)` put the triangle

    T=conv((0,0),(1,0),(0,1)).

At every base `(1,0,j)` put

    R1=[-delta/2,delta/2] times [-L/2,L/2].

At every base `(0,1,j)` put

    R2=[-L/2,L/2] times [-delta/2,delta/2].

At every base `(1,1,j)` put

    R3={s(1,-1)+t(1,1): |s|<=L/2, |t|<=delta/4}.

Let `C` be the convex hull of these lifted fibers. Its integer base set is exactly `P`. At a vertex of the binary square, a convex representation uses only that same binary vertex; along the third coordinate all listed fibers are identical. Thus the stated fibers are exactly the actual fibers of `C`, including the intermediate chain bases. The body has full ambient interior.

The fiber areas are `1/2,1/100,1/100,1/100`, repeated nine times. Therefore

    M=477/100,       k=8,
    max fiber area=1/2 < M/8=477/800.                (1)

All fibers have positive area and all eight parities are occupied.

## 2. Genuine global depth and its critical circuit

Write the continuous coordinates as `(x,y)`, and let `g=(1/3,1/3)`. The point

    Y=(0,0,0,g)

has raw depth exactly `Q=2`. For the lower bound, retain only the nine triangle fibers. Their base distribution is symmetric around chain coordinate zero. The proved paired-centroid-tail theorem (`candidate 732b11a769399016`, Sections 1 and 7) gives raw mass at least `9*(1/2)*Gamma_2=2` in every nonvertical halfspace through `Y`. A pure-integer halfspace through `Y` contains at least five of those fibers, hence has mass at least `5/2`. Moving any containing halfspace boundary to `Y` can only decrease its captured mass.

The following three closed caps through `Y` each have raw mass exactly two:

    H1: x-10(z1+z2)>=1/3,
    H2: y-10(z1+z2)>=1/3,
    H3: -x-y-10(z1+z2)>=-2/3.                       (2)

They strictly miss all rectangle fibers: each relevant continuous linear functional is less than five in absolute value on all three rectangles, whereas the binary penalty is at least ten. On each triangle they are its three centroid vertex caps, each of area `2/9`.

These caps also give raw depth at most two at every point in the triangle column, since their middle traces cover `T`. At any point of a rectangle column, first choose one of two opposite continuous halfspaces through that point that captures at most half that column's mass. The boundary has zero area. A sufficiently large finite exposing tilt at its binary square vertex excludes all other columns and retains the chosen cut in its own column. This gives raw depth at most `9/200<2`. Therefore `Q=2` is the actual global maximum and all caps in (2) are genuine global critical caps.

Their continuous normals sum to zero. Their coarea section measures are all `6`: each triangle contributes `2/3` after division by the continuous normal length, and there are nine copies. Thus the circuit response weights are all `theta_j=1/3`.

## 3. Exact boundary coefficient

Let `eta` be the sum over fibers of ordinary perimeter measure with its outward unit continuous normal `nu`, and put

    W=(1_(H1)+1_(H2)+1_(H3))/3

on these boundaries. Boundaries at cap/facet intersections have zero perimeter, so there is no unspecified allocation. On every rectangle boundary `W=0`.

On each of the triangle's three facets the average of `W` is `4/9`. For example, on `x=0`, the two nonempty traces have lengths `2/3` each; dividing their total by three gives `4/9`. The same calculation holds on `y=0`; on `x+y=1`, both nonempty traces occupy `2/3` of that edge.

The triangle's outward normals are `-e1,-e2,(1,1)/sqrt(2)`. At either of the first two normals, its edge length is one while the rectangle edges of that normal have total length `L+delta`. At the third normal, its length is `sqrt(2)` while `R3` contributes `L sqrt(2)`. Repetition over the nine chain bases multiplies both numerator and denominator by nine. All other normals have zero numerator. Consequently, for every nonnegative normal-only function `psi` with positive denominator,

    integral psi(nu) W d eta / integral psi(nu) d eta
       <= (4/9)/(1+L)=4/81 < 1/18=Gamma_2/k.         (3)

The upper bound is attained by selecting only the diagonal normal. Thus (3) is exact, not merely an estimate using a particular potential.

The obstruction is specifically to forgetting where a boundary normal occurs. The convex nonnegative base hinge

    Phi(z,x)=(1-z1-z2)_+

equals one on the triangle column and zero on the other columns. Its boundary ratio is exactly `4/9`. Hence this example does not obstruct the actual base-dependent convex-potential class.

## 4. Scope of the obstruction

Strict no-heavy volume and genuine criticality do not alone supply the desired normal-only boundary inequality. The stronger minimal-closed-minor premises are absent: the triangle column has mass fraction `50/53` and only two parities, and already gives a much better center. This is explicitly not a hypothetical minimal counterexample. It shows that any proposed common-boundary payment must retain actual base localization or another geometry condition, rather than only the distribution of continuous normals.
